clue.text: Turned on the epidural

parts.note: an epidural injection numbs the spine, so the clue invites a jokey reading of the phrase as something that numbs the back

explanation.surface: A patient in labour has just been switched over to a spinal anaesthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means an out-of-date issue of a magazine, or a person past their best; split as BACK NUMB-ER it is 'a thing that numbs the back', which is what an epidural does.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidural is an anaesthetic injected near the spine, literally a device for deadening feeling in the lower back.

clue.text: Charged as a result of forged note

parts.note: a forged or counterfeit coin is called a bad one
E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: Someone was charged with an offence because of a counterfeit banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' looks like an accusation, but here it means ordered or commanded, the past tense of bid.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone to do something is to command them, and the past of bid in that sense is the same.

clue.text: Exercising can tire on such a vessel

indicators.note: exercising puts the letters through their paces, working them into a new order

explanation.surface: A fitness tip: working out may tire you on board such a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercising' signals the anagram: the letters of CAN TIRE ON are rearranged. 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is any receptacle, such as a can.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel in the sense of a receptacle for holding things, like a jar, tin or box.

clue.text: Patient attention is expected from her

definitions.text: Patient attention is expected from her

parts.words: Patient attention is expected from her
parts.note: read as a hospital worker who attends to patients, rather than someone showing patience

explanation.surface: She is a woman expected to be patient and attentive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like an adjective meaning tolerant, but it is the noun: attention to patients is her job.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital worker who cares for the sick on a ward is expected to give care to those in her charge.

clue.text: A blunder that makes many a one place

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a crossword shorthand for many
I is the Roman numeral one
to place a bet is to stake money

explanation.surface: A blunder that causes plenty of people to put a single item down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' is the betting sense: to place money on a horse is to stake it.
explanation.definitionFit: An error or slip, as in a gaffe made in haste.

clue.text: Totally without purpose?

parts.note: purpose can mean an aim or end, so having no end at all is being without purpose

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about something utterly pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: An end is a purpose (to what end?), so something with no end at all is jokily 'totally without purpose'; the usual meaning is everlasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any end, in the sense of going on forever, read here as having no aim.

clue.text: A request-in principle an order though

indicators.note: in says the letters wanted sit inside the words principle an

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a polite request is, in principle, really an order.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash-joined 'in' looks like part of the phrase 'in principle', but it is the signal that the answer lies within principLE An; 'order though' merely completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest appeal or entreaty is a kind of request.

clue.text: Game responsible for set-to

parts.note: a set of things, as at an auction, is a lot
taken as written

explanation.surface: A particular game is to blame for a fight breaking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set-to' looks like one word meaning a scrap, but the hyphen hides two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A game of chance like bingo, where numbers are drawn and matched to cards.

clue.text: Expertise is needed to dress in a way-out fashion

indicators.note: way-out fashion is outlandish styling, so the words to dress in a get rearranged wildly

explanation.surface: Skill is required to wear avant-garde clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way-out fashion' sounds like dressing style, but 'way-out fashion' is the anagram signal working on TO DRESS IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilfulness or dexterity, the deftness of someone highly practised.

clue.text: Put on airs about French article on English ballet

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the next piece sits beneath what comes before
about means the first piece goes around the French article

parts.note: to swank is to show off or put on airs
la is the French feminine definite article

explanation.surface: Someone showing off talks about a French grammatical point concerning an English ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps the show-off's word around the French article, giving SWANLAK; in this down clue 'on' places the English abbreviation beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's best-known ballet score, about a princess turned into a bird.

clue.text: Foreign currency row with Argentinian leaders

parts.note: a row in the sense of a loud noise is a din

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of the word Argentinian, here its first two

explanation.surface: An argument over foreign money with the heads of Argentina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' is pronounced to rhyme with cow: a racket. 'Leaders' takes the opening two letters, AR, of Argentinian.
explanation.definitionFit: The monetary unit of several countries, including Serbia, Jordan and Kuwait.

clue.text: Drink provided for a bird in a store display

indicators.note: in means the bird is placed inside the rearranged letters
display here suggests setting the letters of a store out in a new arrangement

parts.note: a jackdaw, often shortened to daw, is a bird

explanation.surface: A drink is supplied for a bird in a shop's window display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Display' rearranges A STORE into SOATER, and 'in' puts the jackdaw inside it; 'provided for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizzy carbonated water, a mixer for spirits.

clue.text: Club assessment is steep

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon
a rate is a valuation or assessment, as for local tax

explanation.surface: A golf club's valuation is considered too high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like an adjective for a high price, but it is the verb: to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To soften something by soaking it in liquid, as fruit in alcohol.

clue.text: A woman's aim-no break-up

indicators.note: breaking up the words aim and no lets their letters be put back in another order

explanation.surface: A woman's goal is to avoid a split with her partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break-up' signals the anagram of AIM and NO; the 's is short for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, borne by Ruth's mother-in-law in the Old Testament.

clue.text: This is certainly too small to be right!

definitions.text: This is certainly too small to be right!

parts.words: This is certainly too small to be right!
parts.note: right refers to a right angle of ninety degrees, so this is something under that size

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a measurement is plainly too small to be correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like 'correct' but is the geometric right angle; anything under ninety degrees is too small to be one.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle of less than ninety degrees, in geometry, smaller than a perpendicular.

clue.text: Study fish in comfort

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: Someone reads up on fish while relaxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In comfort' looks like a state of ease; 'comfort' is the verb, to soothe.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe or console someone in distress.

clue.text: It's not beneath the players to appear gloomy

parts.note: what is not beneath something is over it
the cast are the actors in a production

explanation.surface: The actors are not too proud to look miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not beneath' looks like 'not too proud for', but simply means above, OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and grey, describing a sky covered with cloud.

clue.text: Tough character beats back with lash

indicators.note: back means the word for beats is read from the end

parts.note: raps are sharp blows or beats
to tan someone's hide is to beat or lash them

explanation.surface: A hard man strikes back with a whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses the word for beats; 'lash' is the verb to thrash, as in tanning someone's hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone austere and hardy, like a citizen of ancient Sparta.

clue.text: Seed scattered in poor earth called for a lot of water

indicators.note: seed scattered in poor soil is strewn about haphazardly, so the letters of seed and earth are spread into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Seed sown in bad soil needs plenty of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scattered in poor' rearranges SEED together with EARTH; 'called for' looks like a demand but is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A long arm of sea between Africa and Arabia, certainly a great body of salt water.

clue.text: Putting people in the wrong situation results in misery

indicators.note: in places the people inside the legal wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men is a common crossword word for people

explanation.surface: Wrongly placing people in a certain situation leads to their suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is a civil wrong in English law; 'in' puts the people inside it, and 'putting' and 'situation' only dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Agony or great suffering, physical or mental.

clue.text: Fowl at one point grouped in threes

parts.note: a tern is a seabird, loosely a fowl
E, for east, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: A bird at a certain spot is gathered with two others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' is a compass point, here E for east.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical term for leaves arranged in sets of three, like clover.

clue.text: Set ways stuff for remaining young-looking

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Set ways stuff for remaining young-looking (7)': no parse found for the wordplay; possibly an OCR misread of a word, and no source found to confirm it
annotationWithheld.clue: Set ways stuff for remaining young-looking

clue.text: Those beastly overheads!

parts.note: overheads read literally as things above the head of a beast, rather than business costs

explanation.surface: An exasperated complaint about horrid running costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overheads' looks like business expenses and 'beastly' like horrid, but they are the things on top of an animal's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The branched horns grown each year by deer, carried on top of the head.

clue.text: Room will be found for this old Greek

definitions.meaning: a room at the top of a house, under the roof
relating to ancient Athens and its dialect

explanation.surface: Space will be made for this ancient Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: A loft space beneath the roof, and the adjective for classical Athens.

clue.text: Dig up the remains

definitions.meaning: to find or track down something lost
a faint mark or vestige left behind

explanation.surface: An instruction to excavate the remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate by searching, and a small surviving sign of something gone.

clue.text: Serving men followed as told

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers in service
to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: Servants followed their instructions as they were told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving men' looks like servants but means soldiers: RE, the Royal Engineers, a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Recounted or narrated, as a story is related to listeners.

clue.text: Some painters may get put down

indicators.note: some says only part of the word painters is wanted

explanation.surface: Some artists may be put down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' suggests criticism, but means to bury.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury a body in a grave.

clue.text: What we saw with some lassie yesterday

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone recalls what they glimpsed with a girl the day before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is a link; the answer runs across lassIE YESterday.
explanation.definitionFit: The organs of sight are the means by which we see things.

clue.text: Reformed lags swear anyone can see through it

indicators.note: reformed means the words lags and swear are reshaped into something new

explanation.surface: Ex-convicts who have gone straight vow they are transparent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lags' is British slang for convicts; 'Reformed' shuffles LAGS SWEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass objects such as tumblers and vases, which are transparent.

clue.text: Tetchy! But will take exam at Yarmouth

parts.note: a test is an exam

indicators.note: at Yarmouth suggests what stands at the mouth, or start, of the word Yarmouth

explanation.surface: Irritable because someone will sit an exam in the seaside town of Yarmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: The word's own ending, 'mouth', hints that only Yarmouth's opening letter is used; Yarmouth is an English seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritable or easily annoyed, a close synonym for short-tempered.

clue.text: Anything but rough late in the day

explanation.surface: A remark that something far from rough came late on.
explanation.definitionFit: Level or flat, and an old poetic name for the close of day.

clue.text: Covers feasts in the dormitory?

definitions.meaning: decorative cloths laid over a bed
spreads are lavish meals, so these are meals eaten on beds

explanation.surface: Midnight feasts in a boarding-school dormitory.
explanation.definitionFit: Bed throws, punned as meals laid out on beds, as in a school midnight feast.
